title: VMSA-2026-0006: vCenter auth bypass and code execution, ESX VM escape (patch vCenter and ESX)
summary: Broadcom's critical advisory VMSA-2026-0006 fixes five flaws. Two in vCenter let an unauthenticated attacker with network access bypass authentication (CVE-2026-59309) and execute code (CVE-2026-59310). One in ESX lets an admin inside a VM with a VMXNET3 adapter run code on the host (CVE-2026-47876). CISA lists CVE-2026-59310 and the ESX logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 as known exploited.
product: VMware vCenter, ESX, Workstation, Fusion, Cloud Foundation, vSphere Foundation, Telco Cloud

cves.note: vCenter syslog server directory traversal, code execution. CISA KEV since 18 Aug 2026; CISA marks ransomware use as Known.
ESX VMXNET3 out-of-bounds write, VM escape
ESX insufficient logging: an admin can act without being logged. CISA KEV since 28 Oct 2026.

impact: Unauthenticated access to and code execution on vCenter; code execution on the ESX host from a VM; operations on ESX that are not logged.
action: Patch vCenter first if you can, then roll the ESX update through your clusters (fixed builds in VMSA-2026-0006).
affected: Any VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation or Fusion version earlier than the fixed versions in the VMSA, including ESX and vCenter inside VCF, VVF and Telco Cloud.
VMXNET3 issue: only VMs with a VMXNET3 adapter. Broadcom advises updating ESX rather than switching adapter types.
vSphere 6.5/6.7 are not evaluated: Broadcom says to presume they are affected. vSphere 7.0 (End of General Support 2 Oct 2025): patches only via extended support.
fixed: vCenter: 9.1.0.0300, 9.0.2.0100, 8.0 U3k or 8.0 U2f. VCF 5.x: async patch to 8.0 U3k (KB 88287).
Workstation and Fusion: 26H1 (fixes CVE-2026-41703 only, rated Low there).
Patches are cumulative: newer versions also contain the fixes. There are no workarounds.
steps: Inventory versions with PowerCLI: `Get-VMHost | Select-Object Name,Version,Build`, and for vCenter `$global:DefaultVIServer.Version` / `.Build` after `Connect-VIServer`.
Patch vCenter first if you can: the two Critical vCenter flaws need only network access. You can use the VAMI or the normal update mechanism; vCenter Quick Patch is not available for these updates.
Restrict network access to vCenter to admin networks while you patch (Broadcom leaves compensating controls to you).

Roll the ESX update through clusters with vMotion. Broadcom says these updates are compatible with ESX Live Patch where your environment supports it. Run a depot sync in vCenter if the new versions don't show up in vSphere Lifecycle Manager.
Check the vCenter/ESX combination in the VMware Interoperability Matrix before mixing patch levels.
pitfalls: 'Back-in-time' restriction: the 8.0 and 9.0 updates block upgrades to some VCF 9.x versions until a later release (for example 8.0 U3k can't go directly to 9.1, but can go to 9.1.1). Check KB 67077 before patching mid-upgrade.
Not using Enhanced Linked Mode or Integrated Windows Authentication does not protect you.
Engineered systems (VxRail, SimpliVity and similar) must follow their vendor's own patch guidance.
Broadcom's FAQ (last updated 19 Aug) says it has no information about exploitation, but CISA's KEV catalog lists CVE-2026-59310 and CVE-2026-41709 as exploited. Treat it as exploited.
